title: EU tenant tokenized routing authority and rollback procedure
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Background: Customers operating under strict EU data residency requirements sometimes require temporary or permanent routing exemptions (allowlist/denylist) that differ from default tenant policies. Current implementations rely on control-plane changes which are slow, error-prone, and hard to audit. This ticket designs a tokenized routing authority mechanism that allows authorized tenant operators (or Redwood SRE on their behalf) to present a signed, time-bound routing token granting an explicit routing exception. The token is cryptographically verifiable at the edge routing layer and integrates with our fallback model-variant selector so that exceptions remain compliant (e.g., EU-only model variants). This work also defines an operational rollback and revocation procedure for safe emergency undo when a policy token causes regressions or compliance exposure.
goals: Define token schema and signing workflow (KMS/HSM), including TTL and revocation semantics
Implement verifier in routing decision service with minimal latency (<4ms median added) and clear audit events
Integrate token precedence into tier routing and fallback selection so tokenized exceptions cannot force non-compliant model variants
Ship an operational rollback and emergency revocation playbook with automation hooks for Canary and Global rollbacks
non_goals: Long-term UI for tenant self-service token minting (this is phase 2)
Replacing account-level allowlist/denylist DB — tokens are an additive, short-lived escape hatch
technical_summary: Tokens will be JWT-like, signed by a Redwood KMS key with a compact payload: tenant_id, scope (eg: egress-region:EU, model-variant:variant-id), issued_at, expires_at, nonce, and a 'purpose' field. The routing decision service will validate signature, TTL, allowlist membership (tenant allowed to request this scope), and check a revocation Bloom filter that is periodically refreshed from control plane. Token precedence is higher than default per-tenant policy but lower than enforced regulatory blocks. If token requests a model variant incompatible with EU-residency (eg. external endpoint), verifier rejects and emits a policy_violation audit event. Fallback selection will prefer in-region EU-compatible variants; token may widen allowed variants but cannot opt out of 'region enforcement' hard blocks.
acceptance_criteria: Routing verifier validates signed tokens and rejects invalid/expired signatures (unit/integration tests)
End-to-end Canary: 5 customers with tokenized exceptions route correctly in EU region during canary window
Latency impact measured and <=4ms median on the routing decision path across 95th percentile load
Audit logs contain token id, tenant_id, evaluated_scope, decision, and trace_id for every token-evaluated request
Revocation path tested: revoke a token and verify it stops being honored globally within 60s
Security review completed and KMS key rotation plan documented
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Backend-only implementation behind feature-flag; unit + integration tests; no customer-facing tokens
Phase 1: Internal canary with lab tenants: mint tokens via admin tooling; monitor audit events and latency; run synthetic traffic
Phase 2: Limited customer pilot (opt-in) with documented support runbook
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to GA; enable revocation automation and on-call rollback scripts
Emergency rollback: control-plane toggle 'token-enforcement=false' with automatic fallback to per-tenant DB policies; documented runbook and SRE playbook
notes: Design review 2026-03-03: PM asked that tokens should never be able to override 'data residency hard blocks'—implemented as a precedence rule
Security raised concern about long-lived tokens; enforce max TTL 24h for customer-minted tokens, 1h for temporary SRE tokens
We will use a Bloom filter for fast revocation checks; edge nodes periodically fetch signed revocation manifests to avoid central RPC latency
